title: 三國志·蜀志·卷五~卷八 (Sanguozhi, Siku Quanshu, vol. 15 of 23)
shelf_note: Siku Quanshu manuscript of Chen Shou's Sanguozhi with Pei Songzhi's commentary; the title's juan range matches the juan headers seen on the pages (zh-sanguozhi shelf). Pages are 蜀志 juan 5 (Zhuge Liang) and juan 7 (Fa Zheng), plus a 考證 collation leaf.
structure_note: Printed folio numbers were read on only 17 of 169 pages, so the 5 backsteps / 10 repeats most likely come from misread or per-juan-restarting folio numerals (each juan restarts its foliation, and 考證 leaves carry their own), not from scan disorder; the four sampled leaves are in order. 6 pages lack OCR and 8 lack translation.

book_verdict: Right text, accurate transcription of the main text and Pei commentary, and a faithful English; the defects are header garble and one invented remark that the manuscript is corrupt.
reader_summary: Juan 5–8 of the Shu section of the Sanguozhi in the Siku Quanshu copy, with Pei Songzhi's commentary and the Qing collation notes. The transcription is of the right text and largely exact; the English follows it closely. Warn that the running header is sometimes read as text, and once the translation calls that garble a corruption in the original.

title: 三國志·蜀志·卷九~卷十二 (Sanguozhi, Siku Quanshu, vol. 16 of 23)
shelf_note: Siku Quanshu manuscript of Chen Shou's Sanguozhi with Pei Songzhi's commentary; the title's juan range matches the juan headers seen on the pages (zh-sanguozhi shelf). Pages are 蜀志 juan 10–12 (Liu Feng, Li Yan, Yang Hong/He Zhi, Xi Zheng).
structure_note: Printed folio numbers read on 21 of 164 pages; 7 backsteps / 14 repeats are consistent with per-juan foliation and misread numerals, not scan disorder. Sampled leaves are in order.

tr_errors.english: consulted Zhao Zhi ... Zhi said ... Zhi laughed and said: 'To reach that is quite enough for me!'
tr_errors.problem: both 趙直 (the dream interpreter) and 何祗 (the subject) are romanised 'Zhi' with no surname, so the reader cannot tell who laughs, and reads the interpreter as answering his own prophecy

book_verdict: Accurate transcription and a fluent, mostly faithful English; one wrong allusion note and one ambiguous name rendering.
reader_summary: Juan 9–12 of the Shu section (Liu Feng, Li Yan, Yang Hong, Xi Zheng and others) in the Siku Quanshu copy. The transcription matches the manuscript almost character for character and the English is close. Warn that explanatory notes are model-written and occasionally wrong (a misnamed Jin duke), and that two men both called 'Zhi' are not distinguished.

title: 三國志·魏志·卷四~卷五 (Sanguozhi, Siku Quanshu, vol. 3 of 23)
shelf_note: Siku Quanshu manuscript of Chen Shou's Sanguozhi with Pei Songzhi's commentary; the title's juan range matches the juan headers seen on the pages (zh-sanguozhi shelf). Pages are 魏志 juan 4 (Qi Wang, Gaogui Xianggong annals) and juan 5 (Empresses).
structure_note: Printed folio numbers read on 15 of 136 pages; 4 backsteps / 7 repeats fit per-juan foliation and misread numerals. Sampled leaves are in order.

tr_errors.problem: sexagenary day names glossed as 'thirtieth' and 'second' day: jiawu is the 31st of the cycle, and neither is a day of the month; a reader takes these as calendar dates in an annal

tr_errors.problem: 乂 identified as Deng Yang without support (Deng Yang is 鄧颺); low confidence on who 乂 is

book_verdict: Transcription is accurate; the English is good except that the annal page glosses sexagenary days as wrong day-of-month numbers and renames a cited source.
reader_summary: Juan 4–5 of the Wei section: the annals of the three young Wei emperors and the biographies of the empresses, Siku Quanshu copy with Pei's notes. The transcription is of the right text and nearly exact. The English is mostly faithful, but date glosses in the annals are wrong and a cited source title is normalised, so dates and source names should be checked against the Chinese.
